claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic structure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at room temperature.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has approximately 40% room-temperature strain ductility.
The reported TiVNbTa baseline yield strength is approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding approximately 5 at.% W and aging near 1000°C for 4 hours will cause W to partition from the BCC matrix.
The proposed W addition and aging treatment will form a fine dispersion of W-rich nanoprecipitates.
The W-rich nanoprecipitates will be thermally stable at elevated temperature.
W-rich nanoprecipitates will obstruct dislocation motion and provide precipitation strengthening.
Precipitation strengthening will reduce recovery and softening at elevated temperature.
The intervention will raise the 1273 K yield strength from approximately 330 MPa to 450–500 MPa.
The W-doped and aged alloy will retain approximately 40% room-temperature strain ductility.
Preservation of a ductile BCC matrix will maintain the alloy's room-temperature ductility despite precipitation.
The strengthened alloy will improve its function as a heat-transfer intermediate layer between W and CuCrZr and help keep both adjoining materials within their optimal operating-temperature ranges.
Coarse or brittle W-rich phases would compromise ductility and must be avoided through controlled aging.
The modified alloy must remain compatible with the thermal expansion and operating-temperature limits of W and CuCrZr.

contradictions.description: The material_initial_state grammatically assigns the approximately 330 MPa yield strength to room temperature, whereas the baseline and predicted_outcome assign 330 MPa to 1273 K.
